The two angles required to be added are the gray shaded angles: one is at the lower left, and is the supplementary adjacent angle of the interior angle at the left end of the bottom; the other is at the upper right, and is the supplementary adjacent angle of the interior angle at the top right end. Reasoning: Let the interior angle at the lower left corner in the triangle be A, and the interior angle at the upper right corner be B. Since the lower right corner is 90°, and the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, A + B = 180° - 90° = 90°. The lower-left gray angle equals 180° - A, and the upper-right gray angle equals 180° - B. Therefore the sum of the two gray angles is (180° - A) + (180° - B) = 360° - (A + B) = 360° - 90° = 270°.

method.method_draft: Identify the triangle formed by the slanted side, the bottom horizontal segment, and the right vertical segment in the image. The lower-right vertex is a right angle because the horizontal and vertical sides are perpendicular. Let the two unmarked interior angles at the bottom-left and top-right vertices be A and B; then A + B = 90° by the triangle angle sum. Each gray marked angle is the exterior angle adjacent to one of these interior angles, so their measures are 180° - A and 180° - B. Add them: (180° - A) + (180° - B) = 360° - (A + B) = 360° - 90° = 270°.
